newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Prices generally easier at New Zealand wool sale.
newsitem.headline: Prices generally easier at New Zealand wool sale.

text.p: Prices were generally easier at the wool sale in Christchurch on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The provisional market indicator was down 17 cents to NZ$4.56, with the fine segment down 77 cents to $8.12, medium segment down nine to $4.80 and the strong segment indicator down six at $4.23.
2 percent second shear bellies and pieces
The balance was made up of miscellaneous wools. Passings of wool which failed to meet growers' price reserves amounted to 27 percent.
Compared with the last sales in Dunedin and Napier on September 26, merino fleece was 5.0 to 7.5 percent cheaper and halfbred fleece was 1.5 to 3.0 percent cheaper.
Crossbred fleece 37 micron and finer was up to 1.0 percent cheaper, while 38 micron and stronger was generally unchanged.
Second shear was unchanged, bulky skirtings were slightly cheaper and crutchings were generally unchanged.
Principal interest came from Western Europe and China, with limited support from Iran, Australia, India and local mills.
The next sales will be at Napier and Dunedin on October 10.
